▶ WHAT LANDED (4d497614b). madc emitted NO symbol for __attribute__((alias("T"))) — not for MIR's eight exports specifically, for the attribute AT ALL. It had only the REFERENCE half (a reference to the alias resolves to the target's storage — the redirect that binds system-header class statics to their Itanium symbols, UNCHANGED and load-bearing). The DEFINING half — a second symbol of the alias's own name, its asm LABEL when it has one, at the target's address — was never built. A RUNNING PROGRAM CANNOT TELL THE TWO APART; that is how it survived a green suite.
 · Three facts had shared Variable::storage_alias_name; now three fields, one writer each: storage_alias_name (what a REFERENCE resolves to), asm_label (what it is EMITTED under), alias_definition_target (what it is an alias OF). parseFunction was also passing NULL for the attribute's alias-target out-param, so a prototype carrying the attribute after its parameter list dropped it entirely.
 · cir_emit_alias_symbols (src/madc_cir.cpp) emits in object mode beside cir_register_tu_init, after MIR_link. A DATA target is only DEFINED once the capture's module-data walk has placed it, and that walk ran INSIDE the emit entry — after every chance to annotate — so MIR now exposes it as MIR_gen_object_prepare (mir-gen.c/.h); madc calls it only on a TU that declares an alias, so no other emit ordering moves. Upstreamable as-is.
 · GATES: tests/testasmlabelalias.mad (+.flags --std=c17, .expect) pins the reference half, green in JIT/--exe/--obj; scripts/check-alias-symbol-emission.sh pins the DEFINING half with nm against the gcc oracle, wired into fulltest, two negative controls. known_pre_existing_gaps: SCRIPT `value` IS NOT YET THE 32-BYTE madc_value STRUCT (recorded 2026-08-17, owner: not to be taken on now). Symptom: `value f()` returned BY VALUE emits `int f()` and silently returns nothing (exit 0, empty output) — func_def's return-type arm -> type_list -> append_type_specs has no dtARRAY case and falls through to int. That is why php::print_r returns madc::value & rather than madc::value. CORRECTED PREMISE: a C type DOES exist — madc_value (include/madc_api.h:52) is a tagged 32-byte aligned(16) struct, and madc::value merely CONTAINS it plus two unique_ptr members (32+8+8 = 48 = the emitted long long[6]); the opaque-buffer lowering exists because of those OWNING C++ members, not a missing type. MEASURED: _array/_object are private with no friends and all 40 refs are in ONE file (src/madc_value.cpp) — 12 mutations, 28 reads; the cell finalizer is already wired and called from generated code (cir_builder.cpp:25789/25797); the is_array_object sites would mostly RETIRE. HARD PART: the class deep-copies the containers while the cell path shares, so the migration needs copy-on-write at those 12 sites — a semantic change with its own oracled tests. Full write-up: docs/plans/2026-06-12-type-table-value-abi-design.md section 9. Sibling defect, also open: assigning to a `value &` PARAMETER is wrongly rejected ('assignment of incompatible value').

VLA NOT DEALLOCATED ON BACKWARD GOTO: a `goto` jumping back to before a VLA's declaration must deallocate the VLA (gcc/C semantics; gcc-torture 20040811-1.c). madc lowers VLAs as malloc + __attribute__((cleanup)), which frees only on SCOPE EXIT, not on the backward goto re-entering the scope — so a backward-goto loop over a VLA LEAKS one allocation per iteration. 20040811-1.c leaks ~2GB over 1e6 iterations; it passes only when memory is available (it OOM-SIGSEGV'd when the MIR fork's 128MB code-holder reservation reduced headroom — see mir_fork; arch-gated off x86-64, so it passes again). Proper fix: free the VLA at the backward goto. Separate future slice.
